title: Edmund and the Choir
premise: Elodie Dunmore, an exiled storm-caller hiding in a valley where magic cannot follow, takes in a mute child named Edmund who speaks only in a dead tongue and carries a choir's worth of stolen voices in his chest. The court beneath the mountain bought his soul as payment for an old debt Elodie's family incurred, and the debt-collectors are coming to finish the transaction. To save him she must leave the valley that has kept her powerless but safe, relearn her storm-calling in the world above, and descend into the Undercourt to sing Edmund's soul back out of the ledger. She succeeds at terrible cost: her own memories of the valley — and of the family she found there — are struck from the record as the price, leaving Edmund to remember for both of them.
about_author: Jonah Underhill is the pen name of a former church organist turned archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk songs collected from mining towns. They write fantasy about music, memory, and the bargains ordinary people make with power.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Establishes her exile in Hollowmere, a valley where magic dies at the ridgeline, and her quiet life mending nets and avoiding her past. A storm gathers on the peaks but never crosses over. Emotional beat: loneliness mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: A Knock in the Rain
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. During the first storm in years to breach the ridge, a boy of about eight appears at her door, soaked, silent, humming harmonies no child should know. He cannot speak any living language. Emotional beat: wary compassion overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: Edmund
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She names the boy after the carved letters on his belt-buckle. He draws spirals in ash that match sigils from her grandmother's forbidden songbook. At night he sings in his sleep and the candles gutter in rhythm. Emotional beat: dawning recognition that magic has followed him in.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Owes
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, rendered in his strange, formal interior voice. He remembers being sold: his mother trading his soul to the Undercourt to end a famine, his voice kept as collateral in a choir of the indebted. Emotional beat: a child's matter-of-fact grief.

chapters.title: The Debt-Collector's Shadow
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A tall figure in grey arrives in the village asking after 'the asset,' and every clock in town begins running slow. Elodie realizes the valley's magic-dead soil is the only thing keeping Edmund hidden. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Songbook
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She opens the book she swore never to touch and finds her family's bargain with the Undercourt written in the margins: three generations of storm-callers, each paying down the debt. Hers was supposed to be the last payment. Emotional beat: betrayal across generations.

chapters.title: Leaving the Ridgeline
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Elodie and Edmund cross the pass together; the moment they step beyond the valley, her dormant power wakes painfully and Edmund's hum becomes audible for miles. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of becoming oneself again.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Fee
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. On the road they meet Maren, a one-eyed ferrywoman who once sang in the Undercourt choir and escaped with half a soul. She agrees to guide them in exchange for a promise. Emotional beat: first fragile bond of the new company.

chapters.title: Storm Practice
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Maren coaches Elodie through calling lightning again; her control is rusty and dangerous, and Edmund conducts her like a choirmaster, steadying her rhythm. Emotional beat: joy rediscovering her gift, shadowed by how much it costs her body.

chapters.title: The Town That Sold Its Bells
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The trio passes through a town that traded its church bells to the Undercourt for prosperity; the silence there is oppressive, and debt-collectors post notices listing names due for collection. Edmund's name is on the board. Emotional beat: dread made bureaucratic.

chapters.title: Voices in the Dark
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Collectors ambush them at night; Elodie's storm scatters them but Edmund hears the voices of the other sold souls inside the collectors' lanterns, begging. He refuses to run afterward. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into determination.

chapters.title: Maren's Half-Song
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. By the fire, Maren reveals the Undercourt's true nature: a ledger-court where debts are paid in memory and voice, ruled by the Auditor, who was once human. She teaches them the counter-song that can unbind a contract. Emotional beat: confession as trust.

chapters.title: The Mountain's Mouth
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. They reach the gate beneath the mountain, guarded by a door that only opens for someone willing to pay something on entry. Elodie pays a memory of her sister's face. Emotional beat: sacrifice as toll, grief as currency.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The tunnels are lined with niches holding bottled voices, all softly singing. Edmund recognizes his own voice among them and nearly shatters. Maren holds him steady. Emotional beat: horror tempered by solidarity.

chapters.title: The Choir of the Indebted
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. They find the choir: hundreds of hollow-eyed souls forced to sustain the Undercourt's harmony. Among them, Edmund's mother, still paying her famine-debt. Emotional beat: the enemy is not monsters but the trapped.

chapters.title: Audience with the Auditor
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The Auditor offers Elodie a deal: Edmund's freedom if she signs on as the court's new storm-caller, powering its engines forever. It shows her visions of everything she could protect with that power. Emotional beat: temptation aimed precisely at her wounds.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie sees what acceptance would make of her — a keeper of cages — and refuses, tearing up the offered contract with lightning. The Auditor declares the old debt due in full, immediately. Emotional beat: defiance with consequences arriving at once.

chapters.title: The Counter-Song
chapters.summary: All three POVs interwoven. In the choir hall, Maren begins the unbinding song, Edmund lends the stolen voices their own melody back, and Elodie calls a storm inside the mountain itself. Emotional beat: unity — found family functioning as one instrument.

chapters.title: The Ledger Breaks
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Climax. The Auditor tries to erase Elodie entirely; the counter-song turns her memories into the payment instead, striking them line by line as the ledger cracks. Edmund's soul returns to him mid-storm. Emotional beat: triumph purchased with selfhood.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Dark
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The choir is freed, the mountain settling into silence. Edmund, whole for the first time, looks at Elodie and realizes she no longer knows his name. Emotional beat: victory shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Back in Hollowmere, Elodie lives without her past, feeling inexplicable warmth toward a boy who visits weekly and tells her stories of 'a woman who called storms.' Maren leaves the counter-song written down for her. Emotional beat: tenderness without memory.

chapters.title: The First Verse
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund chooses to teach Elodie the counter-song's opening verse — not to restore her memories by force, but so she can choose, someday, whether to read the ledger of herself. She hums along, almost remembering. Emotional beat: hope as an open door, not a locked one.
